description: Raspberry Pi RP2350 (2x Cortex-M33 150 MHz, single-precision FPU, 520 KB RAM; Arm cores only)
ca_bundle_note: Mozilla's CA list (curl's cacert.pem, the one ESP-IDF ships): flick turns it into bl_ca_bundle.h, the TLS trust store of boards with WiFi.
core_note: arduino-pico (Earle Philhower's core), the version releases are built with.
gcc_note: arduino-pico's own toolchain (pqt-gcc), the one Baseline is built with: the same libc, libm and libstdc++.
gcc_download_note: For flick setup (no Arduino IDE): the pqt-gcc build arduino-pico 6.3.2 installs (its package index, tool pqt-gcc 5.0.0-9576866).
cflags_note: softfp, as arduino-pico builds Baseline: floats travel in integer registers through the API table, so the sketch must use the same calling convention.
ldflags_note: Code and rodata share one address window, so the sketch's one flash segment is RWX by design.
libs_note: The RP2350 boot ROM's C functions are not used: newlib supplies memcpy, strlen, ... (the SDK's malloc/printf come first).
defines_note: Not ARDUINO_ARCH_RP2040: libraries would pick code paths for a core the SDK does not have.
usb_vids_note: Raspberry Pi and SparkFun: arduino-pico's USB serial uses the board's own IDs.
stop_detect_note: Baseline parks a sketch spinning in an empty while(1) instead of letting the watchdog roll it back (flick test step 4).
